newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's BCE posts profit gain, plans stock split.
newsitem.headline: Canada's BCE posts profit gain, plans stock split.

text.p: Canada's largest publicly traded company, telecommunications holding firm BCE Inc., posted improved fourth-quarter earnings on Monday and proposed a two-for-one stock split.

Montreal-based BCE said the split was designed to make the share price more affordable for investors after an 18-month price gain. The proposed stock split must be ratified by shareholders at the annual meeting on April 30.
BCE's fourth-quarter net profit rose to C$429 million ($319 million) or C$1.29 (96 cents) a share from C$289 million ($215 million) or C86 cents (64 cents) a share in the same period a year earlier.
Results for the latest quarter included a one-time gain of C$38 million ($28 million) or C12 cents (9 cents) a share.
Fourth-quarter sales rose 14 percent to C$8.5 billion ($6.3 billion) from C$7.4 billion ($5.5 billion) in the same period of 1995.
For the full year, BCE's profit rose to C$1.15 billion ($856 million) or C$3.40 ($2.53) a share from C$782 million ($587 million) or C$2.23 ($1.66) a share in 1995.
The 1996 results included one-time gains of C$125 million ($93 million) or C39 cents (29 cents) a share, compared with C$55 million ($41 million) or C18 cents (13 cents) a share in the prior year.
Sales in 1996 climbed 14 percent to C$28.2 billion ($21 billion) from C$24.6 billion ($18 billion) in 1995.

BCE unit Bell Canada, a local and long-distance telephone carrier, on Monday reported fourth-quarter net income of C$198 million ($147 million) versus C$138 million ($103 million) in the year-earlier period.
BCE Chairman L.R. Wilson said in a statement that "1996 was a year of successful recovery at BCE, with improved results in all major operating units."
He added that "we must, however, achieve continued improvement in 1997. This year's return on equity of 10.6 per cent is clearly inadequate to sustain the growth of the company"
BCE shares were down C10 cents to C$65.65 in Toronto after resuming trading following a halt for the stock split news. The stock was down 12.5 cents to $48.75 in New York.
